author: claude

patch.value: The chunk boundary is an artefact of how the kernel filled the pipe, not of the data. Any decode that treats a chunk as a complete unit inherits that arbitrariness. A streaming decoder holds the incomplete tail until the next chunk supplies it, which is the only way the result is a function of the input alone.
Decoding stdin chunk by chunk corrupts a multi-byte character split across a chunk boundary

readStdin decoded each binary chunk with Buffer.toString and joined the results. A stream splits on byte boundaries, not character boundaries, so a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence straddling two chunks decoded to two replacement characters, one on each side of the split. Piped NDJSON containing any non-ASCII text was silently corrupted, and a truncated trailing sequence was dropped rather than reported.

A multi-byte character split across two chunks is reassembled exactly; a truncated trailing sequence is flushed as a replacement character rather than dropped; both assertions fail when the per-chunk decode is restored; the coverage gate still reports 100 percent.

value.text: Treat every chunk boundary in a byte stream as arbitrary. Decoding per chunk makes the output depend on how the producer happened to flush.

author: claude

patch.value: readStdin decodes binary chunks through a node:string_decoder StringDecoder and flushes the held tail with end(), so an incomplete sequence is carried to the next chunk instead of being decoded as garbage.
Piped NDJSON containing non-ASCII text arrives byte-for-byte identical regardless of where the producer flushed, and a truncated final sequence is reported as a replacement character.

Restoring the per-chunk decode fails only the boundary reassembly test; removing the end() flush fails only the truncated-tail test. Suite: 19 passed 0 failed. Gates: typecheck 0, lint 0, docstring 0 (17 files, 131 declarations), coverage 100/100/100 across 17 files.

message: Fix the chunk-boundary corruption in the async stdin read
